questions.q:
(a) What must the final recording of each performance be like? [1]
(b) Who marks Component 2, and who checks the marking? [1]
ms: (a) a single take, unedited
(b) marked by the teacher and moderated by Cambridge (both needed)
questions.model: (a) One continuous take with no editing. (b) Your teacher marks it, and Cambridge moderates the marks.

questions.q: Name two kinds of work that are not allowed as compositions for Component 3.
ms: an arrangement of an existing piece
a theme and variations on a theme you did not write
work using ready-made loops / ideas that are not your own
any two, 1 each
questions.model: An arrangement of an existing piece, and variations on someone else's theme.

questions.q: Maria plays the flute. For Part 2 (performing with others) she plans to play a flute sonata, with her teacher playing the piano accompaniment. Explain whether this is suitable and suggest a better choice.
ms: not suitable
she would be playing a solo with accompaniment, which counts as a solo, not ensemble playing
Part 2 must show rhythmic coordination and ensemble awareness with at least one other live performer, her part not extensively doubled
better: a flute duet / trio, or a part in a wind ensemble or band where the parts are equally important
questions.model: It is not suitable: a solo with piano accompaniment is still a solo performance. Part 2 must show ensemble awareness and rhythmic coordination with at least one other live performer, where Maria's part is one of the important parts. She could play a flute duet or one part in a wind quintet instead.

questions.q:
Composition 2 must be written to a brief linked to an area of study.
(a) Write a suitable brief linked to Area 5 (Music for dance). [2]
(b) If you submit a written commentary instead of a score, state two things it must include. [2]
ms: (a) states the purpose/style of the dance (e.g. a salsa, tango, EDM track) [1]
(a) gives forces and a plan (instruments/technology, length, structure or tempo) [1]
(b) timings for each section
(b) details of how the music was made / techniques, instruments, structure (on the Cambridge template)
(b) the brief / stimulus
(b) any two for (b)
questions.model:
(a) 'A three-minute EDM track at 128 BPM for a school dance show, made in a DAW with synthesisers and drum machine, with an intro, two build-ups and drops, and a breakdown.'
(b) Timings for each section, and an explanation of the techniques and sounds used (e.g. how the build-up was created).

questions.q:
A student's Composition 1 is described like this: "16 bars for piano. A melody with block chords in the left hand all the way through. It stays in C major. The same 4-bar phrase is repeated four times. There are no dynamics or tempo markings in the score."
Using the composing criteria, explain three weaknesses and suggest how to improve each one.
ms: Use of medium: one texture throughout [1]; vary it, e.g. Alberti bass, unison, melody in the left hand, imitation [1]
Structure: no contrast (four identical phrases) [1]; add a contrasting B section / ABA, with a link or coda [1]
Compositional technique: ideas are not developed / only one key [1]; use sequence, inversion, modulation (e.g. to G major or A minor) [1]
Score/notation: no performance directions [1]; add tempo, dynamics, articulation, phrasing [1]
Ideas: short and simple, limited [1]; write a more memorable motif / second theme [1]
max 2 per weakness, max 6
questions.model: Use of medium: the texture never changes; it could use an Alberti bass in one section and imitation between the hands in another. Structure: the same phrase four times gives no contrast; a contrasting B section in a new key would make an ABA form. Notation: there are no performance directions; the score should include a tempo marking, dynamics and articulation.

questions.q:
A composer writes this one-bar motif in C major, 4/4, crotchets: C D E G.
(a) Write the motif as a sequence one step higher, staying in C major. [1]
(b) Write the motif inverted, starting on C, staying in C major. [1]
(c) Write the rhythm of the motif in augmentation. [1]
(d) Suggest one chord to harmonise the whole bar and explain why it fits. [2]
(e) Name the cadence you would use to end the piece. [1]
ms: (a) D E F A
(b) C B A F (allow exact inversion C B♭ A♭ F)
(c) four minims (each note value doubled)
(d) chord I / C major (C E G)
(d) C, E and G are chord notes; D is a passing note
(e) perfect cadence (V–I)
questions.model: (a) D E F A. (b) C B A F. (c) Four minims. (d) Chord I (C E G): three of the four notes belong to it and D is a passing note between C and E. (e) A perfect cadence, V–I.
questions.tip: Developing one short motif with sequence, inversion and augmentation is exactly what the Compositional technique criterion rewards.
